cues.zh: 你知道你生活中的东西耗多少功率吗？
cues.en: Do you know how much power the stuff in your life uses?

cues.zh: 太好了！
cues.en: Great!

cues.zh: 只不过那并不重要。
cues.en: Except that doesn’t matter.

cues.zh: 我其实很认真——知道你设备的瓦数功率可能有用，在某些情况下也确实重要，
cues.en: I’m actually quite serious - knowing how much power in watts your devices use can be helpful and it does matter in some circumstances,

cues.zh: 但通常远不如这些东西用了多少能量对你生活的影响大。
cues.en: but it’s usually nowhere near as important to your life as how much energy those things use.

cues.zh: 这听起来可能像那种过度较真的执念，但其实不是！
cues.en: This may sound like one of those overly pedantic fixations but it’s not!

cues.zh: 功率和能量是非常不同的概念。
cues.en: Power and energy are very different concepts.

cues.zh: 它们紧密相关，但这不是全部。
cues.en: They are closely linked, but that’s not the whole story.

cues.zh: 而且不幸的是，如果你不熟悉能源术语，我们讨论功率和能量时用的单位可能会非常令人困惑。
cues.en: And unfortunately, the units we use to discuss power and energy can be very confusing if you’re not well-versed in energy speak.

cues.zh: 不过，如果你能真正理解功率和能量究竟如何相互影响，
cues.en: However, if you can wrap your head around precisely how power and energy influence each other,

cues.zh: 我保证你生活中很多事都会变得容易理解得多。
cues.en: I promise a whole lotta stuff in your life gets much easier to understand.

cues.zh: 你可能会以为我要从电讲起，但在那之前，我想先聊聊这个。
cues.en: Now, you might think I’m going to start by discussing electricity but before we get there I want to instead talk about this.

cues.zh: 这是一瓶液态丙烷。
cues.en: This is a bottle of liquid propane.

cues.zh: 以这种瓶子出售时，它通常被用作露营燃料。
cues.en: When sold in this kind of bottle it’s commonly used as a camping fuel.

cues.zh: 丙烷的能量储存在其化学键中，我们可以让丙烷离开瓶子来释放这些能量，
cues.en: The propane has energy stored in its chemical bonds, and we can release that energy by allowing the propane to leave the bottle,

cues.zh: 汽化，并与大气混合，形成含有大量游离氧的空气/燃料混合物。
cues.en: vaporize, and mix with the atmosphere which creates an air/fuel mixture with a good deal of free oxygen.

cues.zh: 当我们点燃这种混合物时，它就会燃烧——这是一种称为燃烧的化学反应。
cues.en: And when we ignite that mixture it burns - a chemical reaction known as combustion.

cues.zh: 燃烧的有用副产品是热，这是能量最基本的形式。
cues.en: The useful byproduct of that combustion is heat, the most basic form of energy.

cues.zh: 以受控方式燃烧丙烷的装置，就是我们利用丙烷储存能量的方式。
cues.en: Devices which burn propane in a controlled fashion are how we make use of the propane’s stored energy.

cues.zh: 像这样的露营炉。
cues.en: Devices such as this camping stove.

cues.zh: 炉子本身极其简单。
cues.en: The stove itself is incredibly simple.

cues.zh: 除了整体物理结构外，它不过是一根管子，通向两个阀门，再供给两个燃烧器内部的喷嘴。
cues.en: Other than its overall physical structure, it’s little more than a pipe which leads to a pair of valves which then feed nozzles inside these two burner elements.

cues.zh: 用这根非常单薄、不太牢靠的调压连接软管玩意儿把丙烷瓶接到那根管子上，
cues.en: Connect a propane bottle up to that pipe using this very flimsy and precarious pressure-regulating hookup tube thingamijig

cues.zh: 接好之后，打开那些阀门，就会让一些丙烷从罐里出来，
cues.en: and once you’ve done that opening those valves will allow some of the propane to leave the tank,

cues.zh: 然后它经过喷嘴，进入燃烧器，在那里与空气混合。
cues.en: after which it goes through the nozzles and ends up in the burners where it mixes with air.

cues.zh: 按下这个点火按钮，它会击打压电晶体，在丙烷/空气混合物离开燃烧器的位置附近产生火花，然后噗的一声就着了。
cues.en: Press this ignitor button which strikes a piezo-electric crystal in order to produce a spark near where the propane/air mixture exits the burners and fwoomp.

cues.zh: 你生好火了！
cues.en: You’ve got fire!

cues.zh: 现在你可以煮任何美味的东西了。
cues.en: And now you can cook your delicious whatever.

cues.zh: 嗯……但用那瓶丙烷，你能煮多少美味的东西呢？
cues.en: Hmmm… but how much delicious whatever are you able to cook with that bottle of propane?

cues.zh: 这是个好问题——答案与能量有关。
cues.en: That’s a good question - and its answer has to do with energy.

cues.zh: 记住，我们燃烧丙烷是为了释放它的能量。
cues.en: Remember, we are burning the propane to release its energy.

cues.zh: 由于我们只能燃烧它一次，之后它就消失到大气中，
cues.en: Since we can only burn it once and then it disappears into the atmosphere,

cues.zh: 瓶中的丙烷量代表了我们可用的总热能。
cues.en: the quantity of propane in the bottle represents the total amount of heat energy that’s available to us.

cues.zh: 全新满瓶时，那瓶装有一磅液态丙烷（即453克）。
cues.en: When new and full, that bottle contained one pound of liquid propane (that’s 453 grams).

cues.zh: 但就是这样——用完了就用完了。
cues.en: But that’s it - when it runs out it runs out.

cues.zh: 那么，在计算一瓶丙烷能做多少事时，有个看似复杂的问题。
cues.en: Now, when it comes to figuring out how much we can do with a bottle of propane, there’s what might seem like a complication.

cues.zh: 如果你以前用过任何炉灶，就会知道我们每次做饭时并不总是用同样的方式。
cues.en: If you’ve used any kind of stove before, you’ll know that we don’t always use them in the same way every time we cook.

cues.zh: 有时我们可能需要烧一大锅水，但其他时候我们可能需要更温和的烹饪方式，比如慢炖。
cues.en: Sometimes we might need to boil a big pot of water but on other occasions we might need to do gentler kinds of cooking, such as simmering.

cues.zh: 为了满足这些不同的需求，炉灶上的阀门可以以不同的速率从气瓶中释放丙烷。
cues.en: To address those varying needs, the valves on the stove can release the propane from the bottle at different rates.

cues.zh: 看——当我把阀门关小、减慢燃料流速时，火焰会变小，也不那么热了。
cues.en: Watch - as I close the valve down and slow the rate of fuel flow, the flame shrinks and isn’t as hot.

cues.zh: 这让我们能够进行那些更温和的烹饪任务，方法是限制锅具在火焰上方时所能达到的最高温度。
cues.en: This lets us do those gentler cooking tasks by introducing a limit to how hot a piece of cookware can possibly get when sitting above the flame.

cues.zh: 但当我将阀门调到全开设置时，燃料流速增加，因此产生的火焰更热（也更大）。
cues.en: But when I set the valve to its wide-open setting, the rate of fuel flow increases so the hotter (and larger) the resulting flame is.

cues.zh: 你甚至能听出这种差别。
cues.en: You can even hear that difference.

cues.zh: 那这种差别到底是什么？
cues.en: And just what exactly is that difference?

cues.zh: 是功率。
cues.en: It’s power.

cues.zh: 通过调节燃料流量，阀门调整燃烧器的功率水平，从而改变火焰的大小和热量。
cues.en: Through adjusting the rate of fuel flow, the valves adjust the power level of the burners and thus the size and heat of their resulting flames.

cues.zh: 关键要注意的是，功率不是瓶子里有多少丙烷，甚至也不是我们烧掉了多少。
cues.en: Critical to note is that power is NOT how much propane is in the bottle or even how much we’ve burned.

cues.zh: 相反，功率是我们在任意时刻烧掉丙烷、释放其能量的*快慢*。
cues.en: Instead, power is how *quickly* we are burning through the propane and releasing its energy at any given moment.

cues.zh: 因此，功率代表的是瞬时的能量强度，这和能量本身不是一回事。
cues.en: Power, therefore, represents an instantaneous energy intensity, which is not the same thing as energy itself.

cues.zh: 为什么这如此重要？
cues.en: Why is that so important?

cues.zh: 因为真正做功的是能量。
cues.en: Well, because energy is what actually accomplishes work.

cues.zh: 把事情做成，比如把水烧开或煎熟一块鸡肉，都需要一定量的能量。
cues.en: Getting things done, like bringing water to a boil or cooking a piece of chicken, requires a certain amount of energy.

cues.zh: 其实你可以算出把六杯室温水烧开需要多少能量。
cues.en: You can actually calculate how much energy it takes to bring, say, six cups of room temperature water to a boil.

cues.zh: 这就是物理事实。
cues.en: That's just a fact of physics.

cues.zh: 我们也知道每克丙烷含有多少能量，所以能精确算出烧开六杯水需要烧掉多少丙烷。
cues.en: And we also know how much energy the propane contains per gram, so we can work out precisely how much propane we’ll have to burn to boil six cups of water.

cues.zh: 这个计算我就不细讲了，现在已经显示在屏幕上。
cues.en: I won't go through that calculation, but it’s on your screen now.

cues.zh: 如果我们假设炉子释放的能量有一半真正进入了锅里的水中
cues.en: And if we assume half of the energy released by the stove will actually make it into the water in a pot

cues.zh: （明火产生的很多热量会绕开锅散失，所以损耗相当大，需要考虑进去）
cues.en: (a lot of heat from an open flame ends up going around a pot so there are pretty heavy losses to consider)

cues.zh: 那我们就会发现，要在这个炉子上产生烧开六杯水所需的热能，
cues.en: then we’ll find that to produce the necessary heat energy to boil six cups of water on this stove,

cues.zh: 大约需要烧掉20克丙烷。
cues.en: we need to burn about 20 grams of propane.

cues.zh: 这大约是一整瓶的5%。
cues.en: That’s roughly 5% of a full bottle.

cues.zh: 所以，关键问题是：
cues.en: So, here’s the key question:

cues.zh: 燃烧器的功率设定在什么档位，这有影响吗？
cues.en: does it matter what power level we have the burner is set to?

cues.zh: 除了微小的效率影响外，没有影响。
cues.en: Aside from marginal efficiency effects, no it doesn’t.

cues.zh: 20克就是20克。
cues.en: 20 grams is 20 grams.

cues.zh: 这就是我们要用的丙烷量。
cues.en: That’s how much propane we’re gonna use.

cues.zh: 烧得多快并不重要。
cues.en: How quickly we burn it doesn't matter.

cues.zh: 然而，这里开始让人困惑了。
cues.en: And yet, here’s where things can start to get confusing.

cues.zh: 当涉及到你我和能源的互动方式时，时间绝对重要。
cues.en: When it comes to how you and I interact with our energy resources, time absolutely matters.

cues.zh: 事实上，时间是理解功率是什么以及它与能耗关系的关键。
cues.en: In fact, time is the key to understanding what power is and how it relates to energy consumption.

cues.zh: 想想看，炉子不允许我们瞬间烧完所有这些丙烷。
cues.en: Consider that the stove doesn’t allow us to burn all of this propane in an instant.

cues.zh: 如果可以，那就不是燃烧，而是爆炸了。
cues.en: If it did, we wouldn’t be burning it so much as we’d be exploding it.

cues.zh: 我们不希望那样，所以炉子限制了丙烷离开瓶子的速度，从而限制了我们释放热能的快慢。
cues.en: We don’t want that so the stove limits how quickly the propane can leave the bottle and thus it limits how quickly we can release its heat energy.

cues.zh: 这台炉子在这两个灶眼上燃烧丙烷的最快速度约为每分钟3.8克。
cues.en: The fastest rate at which this stove will let us burn propane on each of these two burners is about 3.8 grams per minute.

cues.zh: 信不信由你，这本身就是一个功率数值！
cues.en: And believe it or not that right there is a power figure!

cues.zh: 这听起来很奇怪，但每分钟3.8克丙烷确实准确描述了这个功率水平。
cues.en: It’s a very weird one, but 3.8 grams of propane per minute does indeed accurately describe this power level.

cues.zh: 记住，从概念上讲，功率就是我们消耗能量的快慢。
cues.en: Remember, power, at a conceptual level, is how quickly we are using energy.

cues.zh: 既然丙烷是我们的能源，
cues.en: And since the propane is our energy resource,

cues.zh: 那么一个告诉我们单位时间内燃烧多少丙烷的数值，描述的就是功率。
cues.en: a figure which tells us how much we burn over a given period of time describes power.

cues.zh: 当然，每分钟多少克丙烷并不是常规的功率单位，但让我们想想它能告诉我们什么。
cues.en: Of course, grams of propane per minute is not a conventional power unit, but let’s think about what it can tell us.

cues.zh: 虽然可能不容易预测一项烹饪任务需要多少丙烷，
cues.en: While it may not be easy to predict how much propane a cooking task will require,

cues.zh: 但既然我们知道灶眼开到最大时每分钟燃烧3.8克丙烷，
cues.en: since we know we burn through 3.8 grams of propane every minute the burner is set to high,

cues.zh: 那么只要知道我们把这个灶眼开到最大功率用了多长时间，就能确定烧掉了多少丙烷。
cues.en: then if we know how long we’ve been using that burner on high power, we can actually determine how much propane was burned.

cues.zh: 只需把这个功率数值乘以总运行时间即可。
cues.en: It's simply a matter of taking that power figure and multiplying it by the total run time.

cues.zh: 例如，用最大功率的单个炉头烧10分钟，就能算出我们用了38克丙烷：
cues.en: So, for example, using one burner on max power for a total period of 10 minutes will tell us that we used 38 grams of propane:

cues.zh: 也就是每分钟3.8克，共10分钟。
cues.en: 3.8 grams per minute for 10 minutes.

cues.zh: 结论是，只要知道功率数值和运行时间，我们就能获得足够信息来确定用了多少能量。
cues.en: The upshot is that power figures, when runtime is also known, give us enough information to determine how much energy was used.

cues.zh: 当然，我们通常不用每分钟多少克丙烷来衡量，但关键在于，每种功率单位描述的都是同一件事：功率。
cues.en: Of course, we don’t typically use grams of propane per minute but the thing is, every power unit is describing the same thing: power.

cues.zh: 所以它们之间可以互相换算。
cues.en: So you can convert between them.

cues.zh: 这个功率水平也等于4.3马力。
cues.en: This power level is also 4.3 horsepower.

cues.zh: 或者每小时11,000 BTU。
cues.en: Or 11,000 BTU/hr.

cues.zh: 或者略低于一冷吨。
cues.en: Or not quite one ton of refrigeration.

cues.zh: 或者用你可能最熟悉的功率单位，
cues.en: Or, the power unit you’re probably most familiar with,
3,200 watts.

cues.zh: 是的，你可能不知道，瓦特并不专属于电。
cues.en: Yes, in case you weren’t aware the watt is not exclusive to electricity.

cues.zh: 瓦特是功率！
cues.en: The watt is power!

cues.zh: 它可以指电功率，但也可以指热输出或机械功率。
cues.en: It can mean electrical power, but it can also mean heat output or mechanical power.

cues.zh: 难道不是大家都知道1马力等于746瓦吗？
cues.en: Doesn’t everybody know 1 horsepower is 746 watts?

cues.zh: 当然，我们通常是在电器的语境下提到瓦特，所以我想我们应该转而谈谈电。
cues.en: Of course, we usually reference the watt in the context of electrical devices so I guess we should transition to talking about electricity.

cues.zh: 不过首先，瓦特到底是什么？
cues.en: First, though, what exactly is the watt?

cues.zh: 很简单！
cues.en: Simple!

cues.zh: 一瓦等于每秒一焦耳。
cues.en: One watt is equivalent to one joule per second.

cues.zh: 好，焦耳是能量单位，但别担心，你其实不需要知道焦耳到底是什么，
cues.en: Now, okay, the joule is a unit of energy but don’t worry, you don’t actually need to know what exactly the joule is,

cues.zh: 你只需要知道它是一定数量的能量。
cues.en: you just need to know it’s a specific quantity of energy.

cues.zh: 而一秒内用掉多少焦耳的能量，就是……瓦特。
cues.en: And how many joules of energy get used in one second is… watts.

cues.zh: 就这么简单。
cues.en: It’s that simple.

cues.zh: 物理学家们请注意：我知道能量守恒定律，也知道说“被使用的焦耳”在技术上并不准确，但
cues.en: Note to physicists: I am aware of the conservation of energy and that saying “joules which get used” is not technically correct but

cues.zh: 这个视频是为了帮助人们理解他们如何使用能源。
cues.en: this video is to help people understand how they use energy resources.

cues.zh: 所以请大家将就一下。
cues.en: So please just roll with it.

cues.zh: 现在，既然瓦特代表每秒使用的焦耳数，那么就像炉子的例子一样，
cues.en: Now, since watts represent the number of joules used per second then just like in the stove example,

cues.zh: 如果你知道一个设备运行需要多少瓦特，并且你记录了该设备运行了多长时间
cues.en: if you know how many watts a device needs to function and you have a record of how long the device has been functioning

cues.zh: 你就能精确确定该设备在那段时间内实际使用了多少焦耳（也就是多少能量）。
cues.en: you will be able to determine precisely how many joules (and thus how much energy) that device actually used during that time.

cues.zh: 然而，焦耳是非常非常小的能量单位。
cues.en: However, joules are teeny tiny little bits of energy.

cues.zh: 一个十瓦的灯泡每分钟消耗600焦耳。
cues.en: A ten watt light bulb consumes 600 joules every minute.

cues.zh: 好消息是，正如功率就是功率，能量就是能量！
cues.en: Now the good news is, just as power is power, energy is energy!

cues.zh: 我们可以用许多不同的单位来量化能量，但它们描述的都是同一件事，所以可以相互换算。
cues.en: There are many different units we can use to quantify energy but they all describe the same thing so we can convert between them.

cues.zh: 说到电能时，
cues.en: When we’re talking about electrical energy,

cues.zh: 因为焦耳实在太小，而且大多数人对一焦耳到底是多少也没什么概念，
cues.en: because the joule is really tiny and most people don’t have much feel for what a joule is anyway,

cues.zh: 我们通常用一个叫瓦时的能量单位。
cues.en: we usually use a unit of energy called the watt-hour.

cues.zh: 瓦时顾名思义：就是功率的瓦数乘以总运行时长的小时数。
cues.en: Watt-hours are what they sound like: it is simply power in watts multiplied by the total runtime in hours.

cues.zh: 得到的结果就是瓦时。
cues.en: The result you get is watt-hours.

cues.zh: 比如，同样是那个10瓦的灯泡，运行三小时后，会消耗30瓦时的能量。
cues.en: So, for example, that same 10 watt light bulb, after running for three hours, will consume 30 watt-hours of energy.

cues.zh: 10瓦乘以3小时等于30瓦时。
cues.en: 10 watts times 3 hours equals 30 watt-hours.

cues.zh: 很简单。
cues.en: Quite simple.

cues.zh: 顺便一提，因为一小时有3600秒，这意味着1瓦时等于3600焦耳，
cues.en: And, just for funsies, since there are 3,600 seconds in an hour that means there are 3,600 joules in a watt-hour,

cues.zh: 所以30瓦时等于108,000焦耳。
cues.en: so 30 watt-hours is equal to 108,000 joules.

cues.zh: 也许你就明白为什么我们通常不用焦耳了。
cues.en: Perhaps you see why we don’t usually use joules.

cues.zh: 但不幸的是，虽然瓦时这个概念非常简单，计算也很简单，但如果你不习惯的话，可能会有点困惑。
cues.en: But unfortunately, although the watt-hour is a very simple concept and it’s very simple to calculate, it can be a little confusing if you’re not used to it.

cues.zh: “瓦时”听起来和“瓦每小时”危险地相似，这可能会让你误以为它是我们使用瓦特的速率。
cues.en: “Watt-hours” sounds dangerously close to “watts per hour,” and that might land in your brain as a speed at which we use watts.

cues.zh: 但关于瓦特，你必须记住的是，瓦特本身就是一种速率。
cues.en: But the thing you’ve gotta keep in mind about the watt is that the watt itself is a rate.

cues.zh: 毕竟它就是焦耳每秒，
cues.en: It’s literally joules per second, after all,

cues.zh: 所以从某种意义上说，瓦特是一种速度。
cues.en: so in a sense the watt is a speed.

cues.zh: 能量的速度。
cues.en: A speed of energy.

cues.zh: 要从瓦特实际量化能量的大小，我们需要知道我们以那个“速度”运行了多久。
cues.en: To actually quantify an amount of energy from the watt, we need to know how long we've been running at that “speed.”

cues.zh: 瓦时中的“时”，让我们能够确定已知瓦特速率与一小时时间的乘积。
cues.en: The hour, in watt-hour, allows us to determine the product of a known rate in watts and an hour’s time.

cues.zh: 这意味着瓦时既是从功率和时间推导能量的计算
cues.en: This means the watt-hour is both a calculation that derives energy from power and time

cues.zh: 也是该计算的结果。
cues.en: and the result of that calculation.

cues.zh: 我认为，如果你不熟悉能源领域的说法，这正是让人困惑的地方。
cues.en: That’s, I think, what makes it confusing if you’re not well-versed in energy speak.

cues.zh: 用计算来量化能量不仅显得相当笨拙，
cues.en: Not only can it seem pretty clunky to quantify energy as a calculation,

cues.zh: 而且瓦特和瓦时这两个术语在语言逻辑上与我们通常描述速率和数量的方式正好相反。
cues.en: but the terminology watt and watt-hour is linguistically backwards compared to how we typically describe rates and quantities.

cues.zh: 通常，当我们在单位中看到时间成分时，比如英里每小时或每分钟转数，
cues.en: Usually when we see a time component in a unit, like miles per hour or revolutions per minute,

cues.zh: 我们是在通过说明在该时间段内能完成什么来描述一个速率。
cues.en: we are describing a rate by saying what will get done in that time period.

cues.zh: 但因为瓦特本身就是一个速率（焦耳每秒），它能独立存在。
cues.en: But because the watt itself is a rate (joules per second) it stands on its own.

cues.zh: 就像仅凭速度读数无法告诉你行驶了多远，除非知道以该速度行驶了多长时间，
cues.en: Much like a speed reading can’t tell you a distance traveled without knowing how long you’ve been traveling at that speed,

cues.zh: 瓦特也无法描述能量的数量，除非我们把总时间加进来。
cues.en: the watt can’t describe a quantity of energy unless we add the total time to the mix.

cues.zh: 这就是瓦时的意义所在。
cues.en: And that’s the point of the watt-hour.

cues.zh: 虽然它看起来有点笨拙，但瓦时对于理解能量非常有用
cues.en: And although it can seem clunky, the watt-hour is incredibly useful to understanding energy

cues.zh: 因为它把整个问题中的时间因素放到了最核心的位置。
cues.en: because it brings the time part of this whole deal front and center.

cues.zh: 举个例子，假设你有一台功率为150瓦的电视。
cues.en: For instance, say you’ve got a television which uses 150 watts of power.

cues.zh: 如果你想知道它用了多少能量，你需要知道你看电视看了多久！
cues.en: If you want to know how much energy it uses, you need to know how long you’ve been watching TV!

cues.zh: 看了两个小时后，你的电视会消耗300瓦时的能量。
cues.en: After you’ve been watching for two hours, your TV will have consumed 300 watt-hours of energy.

cues.zh: 这其实就是电视开机时使用的150瓦乘以2小时的运行时间。
cues.en: It’s simply the 150 watts the TV uses when it’s on multiplied by its runtime of 2 hours.

cues.zh: 瓦时。
cues.en: Watt-hours.

cues.zh: 很简单。
cues.en: Pretty simple.

cues.zh: 当我们处理小于一小时的时间间隔时，就乘以小时的小数部分。
cues.en: When we’re dealing with time intervals smaller than an hour, you multiply by the fractional hour.

cues.zh: 例如，要计算同一台电视在15分钟（也就是四分之一小时）内使用的能量，
cues.en: For instance, to calculate the energy used by the same TV in 15 minutes, a quarter of an hour,

cues.zh: 只需用150瓦乘以四分之一小时，即0.25小时，就得到37.5瓦时。
cues.en: simply multiply 150 watts by one fourth of an hour, or 0.25 hours, and that gives us 37.5 watt-hours.

cues.zh: 这是一个简单的计算，希望你能看出它如何运作，有点像计分系统，你的设备耗电时间越长，能量总量就越大。
cues.en: It’s a simple calculation, and hopefully you see how it works kind of like a tally system which adds to the energy total the longer your devices draw power.

cues.zh: 既然我们都有很多需要超过一瓦功率的设备，实际上我们通常用千瓦时，也就是1,000瓦时。
cues.en: Since we've all got a lot of devices that need more than one watt of power, in practice we usually use the kilowatt-hour which is simply 1,000 watt-hours.

cues.zh: 只是让数字更小一些。
cues.en: Just makes the numbers smaller.

cues.zh: 如果你查看电费账单，会发现计费依据是你在该计费周期内消耗的总千瓦时数。
cues.en: And if you were to look at your electricity bill, you will find that you were billed for the total number of kilowatt-hours you consumed during that billing period.

cues.zh: 记住，我在这点上会有点啰嗦，这意味着计费依据是你消耗的能量总量。
cues.en: And remember, I’m gonna be a bit obnoxious about this, that means you were billed for the total amount of energy you consumed.

cues.zh: 每当你看到“瓦特”后面跟着“小时”这个词，或者在缩写中字母W后面跟着字母h，
cues.en: Whenever you see the word “hour” after the word watt, or in an abbreviation the letter h after the letter W,

cues.zh: 那你看到的就是一个能量数值。
cues.en: then you are looking at a quantity of energy.

cues.zh: 不是功率数字。
cues.en: Not a power figure.

cues.zh: 说到电费账单，真正重要的只有电量！
cues.en: And when it comes to your energy bills, energy is the only thing that matters!

cues.zh: 电费账单有个星号说明，我稍后会讲，但大多数住宅电费并不受家里用电功率的影响。
cues.en: For electricity bills there is an asterisk there which I’ll get back to, but most residential electric bills are not impacted by the power draw of your home.

cues.zh: 它们只受家里总用电量（千瓦时）的影响。
cues.en: They are only impacted by your home's total energy use in kilowatt-hours.

cues.zh: 这一点至关重要，因为如果你没有“电量优先”的思维，就很容易被功率数字误导。
cues.en: This is crucial to understand because if you’re not in an energy-first mindset, it’s easy for power figures to mislead you.

cues.zh: 比如，我每次谈到电灶台——不管是电磁炉还是传统电炉——几乎都会反复遇到这种情况，
cues.en: For instance, something that I’ve run across again and again pretty much every time I’ve talked about electric cooktops - induction or conventional -

cues.en: is this idea that electric cooking is wildly expensive compared to gas cooking.

cues.zh: 人们这么说是有一定道理的：

cues.en: in general, methane gas is a less expensive source of heat than electricity is.

cues.en: And electric cooktops do indeed need to be hooked up to beefy 40 or 50 amp circuits because they can draw a lot of power.

cues.zh: 如果我家里灶台上的所有炉头都开到最大，灶具的总功率会达到8500瓦。
cues.en: If all the burners on my stove at home are set to high, the stove draws 8,500 watts.

cues.zh: 这是个吓人的大数字，确实是非常大的功率，
cues.en: That’s a scary big number and is indeed quite a lot of power,

cues.zh: 但电费账单看的不是功率！
cues.en: but power isn't what matters to your energy bill!

cues.zh: 而是能量！
cues.en: Energy is!

cues.zh: 而家用灶台和烤箱的特点是，就普通家庭的能源使用而言，
cues.en: And the thing about household cooktops and ovens is that when it comes to a typical home’s energy use,

cues.zh: 它们几乎可以忽略不计。
cues.en: they’re practically rounding errors.

cues.zh: 想一想烹饪的本质是什么。
cues.en: Think for a moment about what cooking is.

cues.en: It's simply heating food. And, yes, sometimes it makes things very hot

cues.zh: 但你只是在加热很小的东西。
cues.en: But you’re only making small things very hot.

cues.zh: 那份热量虽然往往很强烈，却非常集中，这最终意味着它实际上并不是很大的能量。
cues.en: That heat, even though it is often intense, is very concentrated and this ultimately means it’s not actually a large amount of energy.

cues.zh: 还记得刚才说的时间问题吗？
cues.en: And remember that whole time thing?

cues.zh: 除非你在家开餐馆，否则炉灶一天只用几个小时，
cues.en: Unless you’re running a restaurant out of your home, you only use your stove for a couple hours a day,

cues.zh: 如果你不是爱折腾的厨师，可能还用得更少。
cues.en: likely less if you’re not an adventurous cook.

cues.zh: 但如果你家装了温控，那就有台机器全天候运行，维持着一个比今晚晚餐大得多的物体的温度。
cues.en: But if your home is climate controlled, then you’ve got a machine which is running 24/7 to maintain the temperature of a much larger object than tonight’s dinner.

cues.en: To give you some actual numbers, my home’s air conditioner is a little 2 ton unit which only draws about 2 kilowatts (that’s 2,000 watts) when it’s running.

cues.en: But during the height of summer, that thing will run for somewhere between 6 and 12 hours each day.

cues.en: How does that compare to my stove?

cues.en: And when I do it, I use one of my stove’s small, 1,200 watt burners.

cues.zh: 然后我把鸡蛋打进去开始炒，通常五六分钟就炒好了。
cues.en: and once I put the eggs in and start scrambling they’re usually done within five or six minutes.

cues.zh: 一般等鸡蛋开始凝固时，我会把灶眼的火力调小，但为了算起来方便，
cues.en: Now, typically I reduce the power level of the burner once they’re starting to firm up but to make the math easier

cues.zh: 我们就假设这8分钟里灶眼一直开足火力。
cues.en: we’ll just pretend that I run that burner on full power for the entire 8 minutes.

cues.zh: 那么，这用掉多少能量呢？
cues.en: So, how much energy does that use?

cues.zh: 就是1200瓦（也就是1.2千瓦）乘以8/60小时，结果是0.16千瓦时。
cues.en: Well, that’s 1,200 watts (or 1.2 kilowatts) multiplied by 8/60ths of an hour which results in 0.16 kilowatt-hours of energy.

cues.zh: 这不算什么！
cues.en: That is nothing!

cues.zh: 真的只有我空调一天用电量的1%。
cues.en: Literally just 1% of what my air conditioner uses in a day.

cues.zh: 至于这些电要花多少钱，
cues.en: And as far as how much that energy costs,

cues.zh: 就算按每千瓦时0.5美元的离谱电价，炒这些鸡蛋也只要大约8美分。
cues.en: even with a horrendous electric rate of $0.50 per kilowatt hour, it would only cost about 8 cents to scramble those eggs.

cues.zh: 按我平均每千瓦时0.1美元的电价，连2美分都不到，还不如一个观点的价值。
cues.en: With my electric rate which averages around $0.10 per kilowatt-hour, it doesn’t even cost the $0.02 an opinion is worth.

cues.en: Uh, quick note - I calculated these numbers based on my guess of how long it typically takes to scramble eggs with my stove

cues.en: and I overestimated by a lot!

cues.zh: 我喜欢把鸡蛋炒得很干，即便如此，总耗时包括加热冷锅，也只有5分15秒。
cues.en: I like my eggs very dry and despite that the total time spent, including heating the cold pan, was only 5 minutes 15 seconds.

cues.zh: 我还在2分45秒时把灶火调到了一半功率，也就是说这里实际的能耗
cues.en: I also turned the burner down to half-power at the 2:45 mark meaning that the actual energy expenditure here

cues.zh: 大约是0.08千瓦时，也就是80瓦时。
cues.en: was approximately 0.08 kilowatt-hours or 80 watt-hours.

cues.zh: 这只消耗了极少的能量。
cues.en: It’s a tiny amount of energy.

cues.zh: 光是拍摄这段视频期间，我那套布景里的熔岩灯耗能就比这更多。
cues.en: Just the lava lamps in my set used more energy in the time it took to shoot this video.

cues.zh: 当然，炒三个鸡蛋算不上什么费力的烹饪任务。
cues.en: Now, granted, scrambling three eggs is not much of a cooking task.

cues.zh: 但即便是最耗能的烹饪任务，比如烧开大量的水，在家庭场景下也不需要那么多能量。
cues.en: But even the most energy-intensive cooking tasks like boiling huge quantities of water don’t require that much energy in the context of a home.

cues.zh: 假设损耗为25%，在电炉上把四加仑水烧开大约需要2千瓦时。
cues.en: Assuming a 25% loss, it takes about 2 kilowatt-hours to bring four gallons of water to a boil on an electric stove.

cues.zh: 所以即便你每天都这么做，一个月下来所需的60千瓦时
cues.en: So even if you do that every day, the 60 kilowatt-hours that would require over a month

cues.en: would only represent about 6.5% of the average US household’s monthly electricity consumption.

cues.zh: 那些纠结于电炉使用成本的人，坦白说根本不懂能源。
cues.en: People who fixate on the cost to use an electric stove frankly just don’t understand energy.

cues.zh: 或者他们是在兜售文化战争的废话。
cues.en: Or they’re peddling culture war nonsense.

cues.en: Now, to be clear, I’m not trying to sing the virtues of electric cooking.

cues.zh: 我真正希望帮你们理解的，是拥有以能源为核心的思维方式有多重要。
cues.en: What I’m really hoping to help you understand here is the importance of having an energy-focused mindset.

cues.zh: 瓦特为单位的功率数字很少重要，能量才重要。
cues.en: Power figures in watts rarely matter, energy does.

cues.zh: 如果你把能量放在思维的中心位置，这不仅有助于你理解电费账单，
cues.en: And if you put energy front and center in your mind, not only will it help you understand your electric bill

cues.zh: 还能让你更具体地理解，为什么你生活中的机器运行起来要花这么多钱。
cues.en: but it can bring you a more specific understanding of precisely why the machines in your life cost what they cost to operate.

cues.zh: 我真的很想鼓励你花些时间思考这件事。
cues.en: I really want to encourage you to spend some time thinking about this.

cues.zh: 能量不必是个谜，如果你能培养出对它的直觉，
cues.en: Energy doesn’t have to be a mystery, and if you can develop an intuition for it

cues.zh: 那么你就能更好地把握家中基础设施为你带来的机遇，也能更好地应对挑战。
cues.en: then you’ll have a much better grasp of the opportunities available to you with the infrastructure in your home and the challenges, too.

cues.zh: 是时候抛出一个真相炸弹了。
cues.en: And it’s time to drop a truth bomb.

cues.zh: 事实上，决定你消耗多少能量的最重要因素只有一个，而且简单到近乎滑稽：
cues.en: There is in fact just one single most important factor to determining how much energy you use and it's almost comically simple:

cues.en: it’s what you do.

cues.zh: 其实并不复杂，正是你一天里做的事情决定了你消耗多少能量。
cues.en: It’s not actually complicated, it’s the stuff you do in a day that determines how much energy you use.

cues.en: Every time you ask a machine to complete a task for you, it takes a certain amount of energy.

cues.en: And if you don’t have any idea how much energy certain tasks require, you can figure that out!

cues.en: One option is to use a plug-in energy monitor like this which will not only give you a reading of how many watts a device is currently drawing

cues.zh: 还能告诉你累计的能耗，以千瓦时为单位。
cues.en: but will also tell you a cumulative energy consumption in kilowatt-hours.

cues.zh: 一旦你得到这个答案，你就知道了！
cues.en: And once you have that answer, now you know!

cues.en: which they usually list somewhere on them, and how long you need to use them to complete the task in order to give you some idea.

cues.en: I mean, sure my stove has a label on it which tells me its maximum power draw,

cues.en: The area where power labels can trip you up the most is when you’re looking at a machine which is always in use.

cues.en: but your refrigerator isn’t always running.

cues.en: its max power input is for the defrost heaters which require much more power than the refrigeration compressor does.

cues.en: which will tell you how much energy that model typically uses over a year.

cues.en: And this is true for some other appliances as well.

cues.en: which is not always reflective of your particular reality.

cues.en: That is a complication, for sure, but it doesn’t have to feel like one.

cues.zh: 如果你能让大脑习惯先去想实际完成了什么，就会清晰很多。
cues.en: If you can get your brain in the groove of first thinking about what is actually getting accomplished, it can be very clarifying.

cues.zh: 再看一个例子，某种设备需要大量功率才能运转，却未必对你的电费有多大影响。
cues.en: Let’s go through another example of a device which needs a lot of power to function yet doesn’t necessarily have a huge impact on your energy bills.

cues.zh: 美国这边的电动干衣机，加热元件通常运行在4500瓦。
cues.en: Electric clothes dryers here in the US often have heating elements which run at 4,500 watts.

cues.zh: 又是个吓人的大数字，而且如果你看过干衣机那根粗壮的电源线，
cues.en: Again, a scary big number, and if you’ve ever looked at the chonky power cord your dryer is hooked up with,

cues.zh: 你可能会以为干衣机对电费影响巨大。
cues.en: you might assume the dryer has a huge impact on your energy bill.

cues.zh: 它确实可能影响很大，我不想淡化这一点，
cues.en: Now it can, and I don’t want to minimize that,

cues.zh: 但如果你家里有自己的干衣机，那就想一想吧。
cues.en: but if you’ve got your own clothes dryer at home, well think about it for a minute.

cues.zh: 即便家庭成员多、还在不断增加，大多数时候烘干机也只是闲置在那儿，什么都不做。
cues.en: Even with a big and growing family most of the time the dryer just sits there doing nothing at all.

cues.zh: 它不需要通电，所以只要你不是真的在用，它就不消耗任何能源。
cues.en: It doesn’t require any power and thus it doesn’t consume any energy unless you’re actually using it.

cues.zh: 希望这一点很明显：你用烘干机的频率会影响它的使用成本，
cues.en: It’s hopefully pretty obvious that how often you use a dryer is going to impact how much it costs to use,

cues.zh: 但也许不那么明显的是，最能准确反映烘干机对你电费影响的指标，
cues.en: but what’s perhaps less obvious is that the most precise indicator of what your dryer's impact on your energy bill will be

cues.zh: 并不是你用它的频率，甚至也不是它运行多久，而实际上是你放进去烘干的衣物总量和湿度。
cues.en: is not how often you use it or even how long it runs, it is in fact the total amount and the wetness of the laundry you’re drying with it.

cues.zh: 烘干衣物就是你要它完成的工作，
cues.en: Drying clothes is the work you're asking it to accomplish,

cues.zh: 而你交给它的总工作量，将决定烘干机在烘干周期中实际需要让加热元件运行多久。
cues.en: and the total amount of work you throw at it will determine how long the dryer actually needs to run its heating element during the dry cycle.

cues.zh: 你看，加热元件在烘干过程中其实并不是一直运行的，它会开开关关来维持特定温度。
cues.en: See, the heating element doesn’t actually run constantly during a dry cycle, it turns on and off to maintain a specific temperature.

cues.zh: 而且大多数烘干机有不同的温度设置，方便烘干更娇贵的衣物。
cues.en: And most dryers have different temperature settings, helpful for drying more delicate items.

cues.zh: 这些因素意味着它的平均功耗并不是每次负载都一致的，
cues.en: These factors mean its average power draw isn’t consistent load to load,

cues.zh: 但既然烘干机的任务只是让衣服里的水更快蒸发，
cues.en: but since the task of the dryer is simply to get water in clothing to evaporate more quickly,

cues.zh: 衣服里的水越多，烘干机就得给滚筒里的东西加更多热能，才能把它们烘干。
cues.en: the more water in those clothes the more heat energy the dryer has to add to the tumbly thing before they’re dry.

cues.zh: 所以再说一次，重要的是你怎么做。
cues.en: So again, it’s what you do that matters.

cues.zh: 而不是你设备的功耗。
cues.en: Not the power draw of your devices.

cues.zh: 这几乎适用于你生活中的一切，不管它用什么能源。
cues.en: And that goes for nearly everything in your life, regardless of its energy source.

cues.zh: 有些事你未必能控制多少。
cues.en: There are some things you’re not necessarily in much control of.

cues.zh: 比如，你控制不了天气，所以保持家里温暖或凉爽所需的能量每天都不一样。
cues.en: You can’t control the weather, for example, so how much energy is necessary to keep your home warm or cool varies from day to day.

cues.zh: 但你选择的室内温度会影响所需的能量。
cues.en: But the indoor temperature you choose to maintain will impact how much energy is required.

cues.zh: 而对于生活中那些只有使用时才运行的设备，
cues.en: And for the devices in your life which don’t run unless you’re using them,

cues.zh: 你让它们做的工作量是决定这些设备需要多少能量的主要因素。
cues.en: the work you ask them to do is the main factor to how much energy those devices need.

cues.zh: 你做多少饭、洗多少次热水澡、洗多少衣服，
cues.en: How much food are you cooking, how many hot showers do you take, how much laundry are you doing,

cues.zh: 甚至一辆车的能耗也取决于你实际开了多远，
cues.en: heck even a car uses energy based on how much you actually drive it

cues.zh: 所以“我加了多少油”这个问题的答案，主要取决于你每天实际开车开了多远。
cues.en: so the answer to "how much gas am I buying?" is pegged mainly to how far you actually drive your car every day.

cues.zh: 我这个视频的真诚目标是强调“能量优先”思维的重要性，
cues.en: My sincere goal with this video is to stress the importance of an energy-first mindset,

cues.zh: 到现在，我希望你能看出能量比功率重要得多。
cues.en: and by now I hope you see how energy matters much more than power.

cues.zh: 不过，功率在某些场合确实很重要。
cues.en: However, power levels do matter on some occasions.

cues.zh: 哪些场合？
cues.en: What are those?

cues.zh: 基本上，功率会在三种情况下变得重要。
cues.en: Well, there are basically three ways power can become significant.

cues.zh: 第一种就是我们一直在讨论的：
cues.en: The first is the one we’ve been dancing with this whole time:

cues.zh: 时间。
cues.en: Time.

cues.zh: 功率更大的设备能更快完成工作。
cues.en: More powerful devices can accomplish their work more quickly.

cues.zh: 比如，600瓦的微波炉爆一袋爆米花所需的时间是1,200瓦微波炉的两倍。
cues.en: For instance, a 600 watt microwave oven will take twice as long to pop a bag of popcorn as a 1,200 watt microwave oven.

cues.zh: 两者完成这项任务所消耗的能量差不多，
cues.en: They will both use a similar amount of energy to complete that task,

cues.zh: 但因为1,200瓦的微波炉能更快地把能量送入爆米花，所以它大约只需一半的时间就能完成。
cues.en: but because the 1,200 watt microwave can pump energy into the popcorn more quickly, it will finish the job in roughly half the time.

cues.zh: 同样，英国那种3千瓦的电水壶烧水的时间，是我们这边1,500瓦电水壶的一半。
cues.en: Similarly, the 3 kilowatt kettles they’ve got in the UK can boil water in half the time that our 1,500 watt kettles over here can.

cues.zh: 但能量就是能量，水就是水，所以它们之间唯一的区别就是完成工作的速度。
cues.en: But energy is energy and water is water, so the only difference between them is the speed at which they finish the job.

cues.zh: 它们做这件事消耗的能量是一样的。
cues.en: They both use the same amount of energy to do it.

cues.zh: 当我们做的事情需要更多能量时，功率水平对速度就变得尤为重要。
cues.en: Power levels become especially important to speediness when what we’re doing requires larger quantities of energy.

cues.zh: 比如，我有一辆电动汽车。
cues.en: For instance, I have an electric car.

cues.en: It’s a Hyundai.

cues.en: And it's got a 77.4 kilowatt-hour battery pack.

cues.zh: 你听到了“瓦”后面的“时”，所以这个数字告诉我们电池组能储存多少能量。
cues.en: Now, you heard "hour" after "watt" so that figure is telling us how much energy the battery pack can store.

cues.zh: 这能量可不小。
cues.en: And that’s a good deal of energy.

cues.zh: 你看出功率会如何影响给电池充满电所需的时间了吗？
cues.en: And do you see how power is going to impact how long it takes to refill that battery?

cues.zh: 我家的充电器能提供7.5千瓦的功率。
cues.en: My home charger can deliver 7.5 kilowatts of power.

cues.zh: 所以，小测验：我的7.5千瓦充电器每小时能给车充多少千瓦时？
cues.en: So, pop quiz, how many kilowatt-hours can my 7.5 kilowatt charger supply to the car every hour?

cues.zh: 这并不难。
cues.en: It's not a hard one.

cues.zh: 那么，用我的7.5千瓦充电器给车充电需要多少小时？
cues.en: So how many hours does it take to charge my car with my 7.5 kW charger?

cues.zh: 很简单，把电池能储存的77.4千瓦时能量除以充电器能提供的7.5千瓦功率，
cues.en: That’s easy, divide the 77.4 kilowatt-hours of energy the battery can store by the 7.5 kilowatts of power my charger can deliver

cues.zh: 就得到10.32小时。
cues.en: and we get 10.32 hours of time.

cues.zh: 但那是从完全没电充到满电的时间，我其实从来不需要这么做。
cues.en: But, that would be a completely empty-to-full charging time which I’ve never actually needed to do.

cues.zh: 我还忽略了效率问题，不过整个视频里我一直都在忽略它！
cues.en: I’ve also ignored efficiency but I’ve been doing that this entire video!

cues.zh: 最后我们会提到这一点。
cues.en: We’ll touch on it at the end.

cues.zh: 电动汽车爱好者之所以痴迷于直流快充能输出的功率数字，
cues.en: The reason electric car nerds are obsessed with the power numbers DC fast chargers can put out

cues.zh: 正是因为功率越大，能量传输越快，也就意味着缩短了电池组充电所需的时间。
cues.en: is precisely because the more powerful they are the more quickly they deliver energy, which means they shorten the time it takes to recharge a battery pack.

cues.zh: 我不想过分纠结这一点，因为这里有诸多因素在起作用，包括各个车型和具体的充电设备，
cues.en: I don’t want to get too fixated on this because there are many factors at play here between individual car models and specific charging equipment,

cues.zh: 但我的车在充电器功率足够大时，能在18分钟内从10%充到80%，
cues.en: but the reason my car can charge from 10% to 80% in 18 minutes when it’s on a sufficiently powerful charger

cues.zh: 是因为在这样的充电过程中，它的电池包平均能接受约170千瓦的功率输入。
cues.en: is because its battery pack can accept an average power input of about 170 kilowatts in such a charging session.

cues.zh: 这是相当惊人的功率，需要在直流快充站配备大规模的电网接入，
cues.en: That is a bonkers amount of power which requires a significant grid hookup at a DC fast charging site,

cues.zh: 但实际上这并不是巨大的能量。
cues.en: but it’s not actually a huge amount of energy.

cues.zh: 大约只有52千瓦时。
cues.en: It’s only about 52 kilowatt-hours.

cues.zh: 我家的充电器因为功率受限，需要大约7小时才能提供相同的能量——让车从10%充到80%，
cues.en: My charger at home, since it’s power limited, needs roughly 7 hours to deliver the same amount of energy - taking the car from 10% to 80%.

cues.zh: 但能量总量是一样的。
cues.en: but it’s still the same amount of energy.

cues.zh: 功率更大只是加快充电速度，这对公路旅行或需要快速补电时很重要，
cues.en: More power just speeds up charging, which is important on a road trip or if you need a quick charge,

cues.zh: 但并不会改变汽车行驶一定距离所需的能量。
cues.en: but it doesn’t change how much energy a car needs to drive a certain distance.

cues.zh: 说完了给大电池充电，
cues.en: Moving on from charging big batteries,

cues.zh: 功率重要的第二种情形要关键得多，那就是当我们有功率上限时。
cues.en: the second way power can matter is much more significant, and that is when we have a power limit.

cues.zh: 你们听我讲过电力服务容量等级。
cues.en: You’ve heard me talk about electric service levels before.

cues.zh: 它们通常用安培来描述，原因跟一根电线能安全通过多少电流有关，
cues.en: They’re usually described in terms of amps for reasons having to do with how much current you can safely send through a wire

cues.zh: 但安培上限也是一种功率上限。
cues.en: but an amperage limit is also a power limit.

cues.zh: 我家是100安培的电力服务，这意味着在主断路器有跳闸风险之前，我家能取用的最大功率约为20千瓦。
cues.en: I have 100 amp service in my home which means that the most power my home can draw before the main breaker is at risk of tripping is about 20 kilowatts.

cues.zh: 这个上限主要意味着我同一时间只能做有限的事情。
cues.en: The main thing that limit means is that I can only do so much stuff at the same time.

cues.zh: 不过，一天只有24小时，所以功率上限最终也是能量上限。
cues.en: However, since there are only 24 hours in a day, a power limit is ultimately also an energy limit.

cues.zh: 用100安培的供电，我每天最多只能用480千瓦时的电。
cues.en: With 100 amp service I can only consume 480 kilowatt-hours of energy per day.

cues.zh: 但呃，我平均每个月用的电也就比这多一点
cues.en: But, uh, I barely use more than that in the average month

cues.zh: 所以它对我唯一的实际限制，就是我能同时运行多少台设备。
cues.en: so the only practical limitation it presents to me is how many devices I can have operating at the same time.

cues.zh: 也就是说，除非我家真的需要那么多电，以至于20千瓦的功率都满足不了需求。
cues.en: That is, unless my home actually required so much energy that 20 kilowatts of power couldn’t fulfill its needs.

cues.zh: 我知道这对我来说永远不会发生，因为我住的是联排别墅，
cues.en: I know that’s never gonna happen for me because I live in a townhome,

cues.zh: 但如果我有一栋用电取暖的浮夸豪宅，
cues.en: but if I had a grotesque McMansion which was heated by electricity,

cues.zh: 那么在芝加哥地区最冷的冬夜，20千瓦的功率可能都不足以让房子保持温暖。
cues.en: then on the coldest winter nights we face in Chicagoland 20 kilowatts might not be enough power to keep the house warm.

cues.zh: 大房子热量损失更大，外面越冷，散热越快，
cues.en: Big houses have bigger heat losses and the colder it is outside the faster they lose heat,

cues.zh: 所以如果大房子的散热速度超过20千瓦功率所能补充的速度，房子就暖不起来。
cues.en: so if a big house is losing heat faster than 20 kilowatts of power can replace it, the house won’t stay warm.

cues.zh: 就算20千瓦刚好够在外面零下15度时维持室内温暖舒适的温度，
cues.en: And even if 20 kilowatts was just enough to maintain a toasty warm temp inside when it’s -15 outside,

cues.zh: 你也需要一些余量来供其他东西使用，比如照明、电器等等——这就是为什么那些较大的住宅配有更大的电力服务。
cues.en: well you need some overhead for other things like lights, appliances, and whatnot - which is why those larger homes have larger electrical services.

cues.zh: 简单说一句：我们刚才讲的正是为什么了解你家实际的供暖和制冷需求很重要。
cues.en: Quite note: what we just talked about is why it’s important to know your home’s actual heating and cooling needs.

cues.zh: 我做过一个关于HVAC系统选型的视频，而HVAC系统语境下的“大小”其实指的是功率输出。
cues.en: I made a video about HVAC system sizing and really what “size” means in the context of HVAC systems is power output.

cues.zh: 给房子供暖，本质上就是补充从墙壁和窗户泄漏出去的热能，
cues.en: Heating a home is really just an exercise in replacing the heat energy that leaked out of it through walls and windows,

cues.zh: 而能量流失的速率是一个功率数值，因此它能告诉你需要多少功率来补充这些热量。
cues.en: and the rate at which that energy leaves is a power figure, and therefore it tells you how much power you need to replace that heat.

cues.zh: 通过测试，我确定我家在室外零下10度时，只需持续5千瓦的电力就能维持室内69华氏度。
cues.en: Through testing I determined my home only needs a sustained 5 kilowatts of power to maintain 69 degrees Fahrenheit inside when it’s -10 outside.

cues.zh: 所以我有信心，我家永远不需要升级供电容量——我20千瓦的功率上限还留有充足的余量。
cues.en: That's why I’m confident my home won’t ever need a service upgrade - my power limit of 20 kilowatts still leaves plenty of overhead.

cues.zh: 如果你们想知道测试是怎么做的，我会把那个视频链接放上来。
cues.en: I’ll link that video if you want to know how that testing happened

cues.zh: 长话短说，我家需要的热能远低于我炉子规格所暗示的量。
cues.en: but long story short, my home needs significantly less heat energy then the size of my furnace would suggest.

cues.zh: 但即便在单个住宅内，功率上限有时也会成为障碍。
cues.en: But even within an individual dwelling, power limits sometimes get in the way.

cues.zh: 你不仅有整栋房子的供电容量限制，
cues.en: You don’t just have the service level limitation of your entire home,

cues.zh: 你家里每条单独电路能抽取的功率也是有限的。
cues.en: you can only draw so much power from each individual electrical circuit inside your home.

cues.zh: 在美国，这通常是1800瓦或2400瓦，取决于具体电路。
cues.en: Here in the US this is generally gonna be either 1,800 watts or 2,400 watts depending on the circuit.

cues.zh: 这就限制了你家里每个区域能精确做到的事情。
cues.en: And that puts a limit on what precisely you can do in each area of your home.

cues.zh: 通常这些功率限制在厨房之外没那么重要，
cues.en: Usually these power limits don’t matter all that much outside of the kitchen,

cues.zh: 如果你家是最近50年左右建的，厨房里可能至少有两个电路。
cues.en: and if your home was built in the last 50 years or so you probably have at least two circuits in the kitchen anyway.

cues.zh: 但如果你曾在使用便携式空调或取暖器时遇到过断路器跳闸，
cues.en: But if you’ve ever had a circuit breaker trip on you when running a portable air conditioner or heater,

cues.zh: 那你就会亲身发现功率限制的重要性。
cues.en: then you’ll have discovered firsthand the significance of a power limit.

cues.zh: 超载太久，断路器就会跳闸，防止电线过热导致房子烧毁。
cues.en: Go over it for too long and the circuit breaker will trip to keep your house from burning down due to overheating electrical wires.

cues.zh: 所以，有断路器是好事！
cues.en: So, it's a good thing that there are circuit breakers!

cues.zh: 但它们是一种限制。
cues.en: But they're a limit.

cues.zh: 不过要说明的是，功率限制通常只影响你同时能做多少事，以及/或者你做某件特定事情的速度。
cues.en: To be clear, though, power limits generally only affect how much you can do at the same time and/or how quickly you can do any particular thing.

cues.zh: 只有当你的用电需求真的超过限功率电路所能提供的能量时，它们才会成为限制。
cues.en: They only become limitations on what you can do if you actually need more energy than a power-limited circuit can provide.

cues.zh: 而24小时内，即便是标准的15安培插座也能提供36千瓦时的电能，
cues.en: And since over 24 hours even a standard 15 amp receptacle can deliver 36 kilowatt-hours of energy,

cues.zh: 这在典型家庭环境中通常是相当罕见的情况。
cues.en: that’s generally quite a rare occurrence in a typical household environment.

cues.zh: 如果你经常遇到这个问题，那要么是你家设计有缺陷，要么就是你有……非典型的需求。
cues.en: And if you are running into that issue a lot, what you’ve got is either a design flaw in your home or you have… atypical needs.

cues.zh: 好，功率水平会重要的第三种方式，且这是电力特有的，与需量电费有关。
cues.en: OK, so the third way power levels can matter, and this is specific to electricity, has to do with demand charges.

cues.zh: 电表过去完全是模拟的旋转装置，只能记录千瓦时，
cues.en: Electric meters used to be fully analog spinning things which could only log kilowatt-hours,

cues.zh: 抄表员——一个真人——每月会到你家用现场看一眼，然后把显示屏上的数字记下来。
cues.en: and a meter reader—a human person—would swing by your house each month, actually look at it, and then write down the numbers on the display.

cues.zh: 但如今这些已经很少见了。
cues.en: But these days those are rare.

cues.zh: 如今的电表是电子设备，可以逐分钟记录用电量，并通过无线网状通信网络将用电数据上报给电力公司。
cues.en: Electric meters of today are electronic devices which can log minute-by-minute usage and report that usage to the utility through a wireless mesh communications network.

cues.zh: 某些电力公司可能会根据你住宅在特定时段的最大功率消耗（千瓦）来收取费用。
cues.en: And certain utilities may assess a charge based on the maximum power draw in kilowatts of your home at a particular time.

cues.zh: 他们这样做是因为电网管理非常困难
cues.en: They do this because managing the electric grid is very difficult

cues.zh: 而且同时使用的电力越多，电网上的所有发电机就越难工作来供应这些电力。
cues.en: and the more power is being used at once, the harder all the generators on the grid have to work to supply that power.

cues.zh: 因此，有时会存在收费结构，试图让电力用户在用电高峰时段降低功率消耗。
cues.en: So fee structures sometimes exist in an attempt to get electricity customers to lower their power draw during periods of high demand.

cues.zh: 然而，需量电费完全取决于你居住的地方、你的电力公司以及电力公司的政策。
cues.en: However, demand charges are entirely dependent on where you live, your utility company, and your utility company’s policies.

cues.zh: 在美国，居民用电很少收需量电费。
cues.en: Here in the US, demand charges are rare in residential service.

cues.zh: 通常只按千瓦时计费。
cues.en: You’re usually only billed by the kilowatt-hour.

cues.zh: 许多电力公司允许用户自愿选择某些方案，比如在电力公司要求时降低用电需求，就能获得账单抵扣。
cues.en: Many utilities allow people to opt-in to certain schemes, for instance giving folks a bill credit if they lower their power demand when the utility requests them to.

cues.zh: 但强制性需量电费在居民侧相当少见。
cues.en: But mandatory demand charges are pretty rare on the residential side.

cues.zh: 另一方面，商业客户则经常被强制收取需量电费。
cues.en: Commercial customers, on the other hand, they often are assessed a mandatory demand charge.

cues.zh: 比如在办公室，我的电费账单上有一项有趣的每千瓦11美元的费用，
cues.en: For instance here at the office my electric bill comes with a fun $11 per kilowatt fee,

cues.zh: 它取决于每月午间高峰时段电表记录到的最高功率。
cues.en: determined by the highest power draw my meter saw during the midday on-peak period each month.

cues.zh: 太棒了，我爱死它了！
cues.en: It’s great, I love it!

cues.zh: 不过——如果你要交需量电费，就该弄清楚它到底是怎么算的。
cues.en: But - if you are subject to demand charges, you should find out how exactly they are assessed.

cues.zh: 比如，用微波炉加热两分钟，不太可能触发需量电费。
cues.en: It’s unlikely that, say, using the microwave for two minutes is going to kick off a demand charge.

cues.zh: 更可能的情况是，电力公司看的是一个15分钟、甚至20分钟的滑动窗口，如果你有需量电费的话，
cues.en: What’s more likely is that the utility looks at a moving window of 15, maybe 20 minutes and your demand charges, if you have them,

cues.zh: 它是按那个窗口内的平均功率消耗来计算的。
cues.en: are calculated by the average power draw during that window.

cues.zh: 但我不了解你的具体情况，我只是鼓励你去查一查。
cues.en: But I don’t know what your situation is, I’m just encouraging you to look into that.

cues.zh: 不少欧洲人提到他们的账单里包含这项费用，但在水壶功率动辄两三千瓦的地方，
cues.en: A bunch of Europeans have mentioned that their bills include them, but in the land where kettles run at 2 or 3 thousand watts

cues.zh: 我觉得实际情况并没有一些人以为的那么精细。
cues.en: I don’t think they’re quite as granular as some folks seem to think they are.

cues.zh: 最后，我们来谈谈效率。
cues.en: And on a closing note, it’s time to talk about efficiency.

cues.zh: 确实，同一台设备完成给定任务，所需的能量基本总是一样的，
cues.en: It is true that the same device will always require essentially the same amount of energy to complete a given task,

cues.zh: 但换一台设备，可能用更少的能量完成同样的任务。
cues.en: but a different device may be able to do the same task while using less energy.

cues.zh: 这就是能源效率的核心要义。
cues.en: That’s the gist of energy efficiency.

cues.zh: 我们希望尽可能少浪费能源，
cues.en: We want to waste as little energy as possible,

cues.zh: 为此我们取得了巨大进步，设计出的设备能在相同能耗下产出更多有用的功。
cues.en: and we’ve made great strides to that end by designing devices which produce more useful work with the same amount of energy.

cues.zh: 毫无疑问，我们在效率上最大的飞跃来自不起眼的灯泡。
cues.en: Undoubtedly the largest leap we’ve made in efficiency comes from the humble light bulb.

cues.zh: 我小时候，白炽灯还是主流，这意味着大多数灯泡用40或60瓦，还有不少用得更多。
cues.en: When I was a kid, incandescent light bulbs were still the norm, and this meant most light bulbs used 40 or 60 watts, with plenty using more than that.

cues.zh: 单个灯泡并不需要那么多电，
cues.en: Each individual light bulb didn’t need all that much power,

cues.zh: 但通常你至少会同时亮着几个，很快就积少成多了。
cues.en: but you’d usually have at least a few burning at the same time and that quickly added up.

cues.zh: 回想我童年的厨房，光那个房间就有四个60瓦的灯泡。
cues.en: Thinking back to my childhood kitchen, that room alone had four 60 watt light bulbs.

cues.zh: 这意味着这些灯亮20分钟消耗的能量，就跟我炒鸡蛋用的能量一样多。
cues.en: An this meant the lights used the same amount of energy in just 20 minutes as it took to scramble my eggs.

cues.zh: 不过如今，照明技术已经进步到现代灯泡只需十分之一的电量就能产生同样的光。
cues.en: These days, though, lighting technology has advanced to the point that modern light bulbs need as little as 1/10th as much electricity to produce the same amount of light.

cues.zh: 这很棒，意味着照明在电费中的比重不再那么大了。
cues.en: This is fantastic and has meant lighting is no longer that significant to energy bills.

cues.zh: 而且，由于现代灯泡产生的废热少得多，它们也降低了冷却所需的能耗。
cues.en: And, since modern light bulbs don’t produce nearly as much waste heat, they’ve also reduced the energy required for cooling.

cues.zh: 然而，在其他领域
cues.en: However, in other areas

cues.zh: 其实已经没有多少效率提升空间了。
cues.en: there isn’t actually much more efficiency to be found.

cues.zh: 在处理电力时，情况有点奇怪。
cues.en: When we’re dealing with electricity, things are a little weird.

cues.zh: 电力所做的一些事情是完全高效的。
cues.en: Some things electricity does are perfectly efficient.

cues.zh: 电阻加热就是如此——加热元件消耗的每一瓦时都以热量形式释放到环境中。
cues.en: This is the case for electric resistive heat - every single watt-hour a heating element consumes is released into its environment as heat.

cues.zh: 比如，我用炉灶时，唯一的热损失来自加热元件与炊具之间不完美的热传递。
cues.en: So, for example, when I use my stove, the only heat losses are the result of imperfect heat transfer between the heating elements and the cookware.

cues.zh: 但发电并不是100%高效的。
cues.en: But electricity generation is not 100% efficient.

cues.zh: 发电厂燃烧燃料时，只有部分热能被发电机成功捕获并转化为电能。
cues.en: Only some of the thermal energy in a fuel being burned in a power plant is successfully captured by a generator and converted to electrical energy.

cues.zh: 当然，这不是你能控制的，
cues.en: Of course that’s not something you have control of,

cues.zh: 但这也是我们努力提高发电效率的原因之一。
cues.en: but it’s one reason we’re working to make electricity generation more efficient.

cues.zh: 幸运的是——不知道你听说过没有——
cues.en: Luckily - I don't know if you're heard this -

cues.zh: 我们发现了这项技术：你只需造一次设备，把它放在野外，它就能免费收集太阳能或风能！
cues.en: we discovered this technology where you can build a device one time, stick it in a field, and then it collects energy from the sun or wind for free!

cues.zh: 多妙的概念，免费！而且放在野外，可比不断花钱雇人寻找化石燃料、
cues.en: What a concept, free! And sitting in a field sounds much easier than constantly having to pay people to search for fossil fuels,

cues.zh: 开采、提纯，最后还要把它们运遍全国，只为把这一通辛苦的成果喂给发电机
cues.en: extract them, purify them, and finally move them across the country just so we can feed the result of all that hard work to a generator

cues.zh: 让燃料烧掉、消散到大气中，
cues.en: where the fuel gets burned up and disappears into the atmosphere,

cues.zh: 这意味着我们得永远这么干下去，否则发电机就会停转，再也没有电了！
cues.en: meaning we have to keep doing it forever or the generator will stop and no more electricity!

cues.zh: 说实话，我真不明白为什么还得解释：没错，制造太阳能板、风力涡轮机和电池确实需要付出努力，
cues.en: I honestly don’t know why I have to explain that while yes, it does take effort to manufacture solar panels and wind turbines and batteries,

cues.zh: 但你只需要做一次，之后就能免费获得几十年的能源，不需要任何投入！
cues.en: you only do that one time and then you get decades of free energy from them with no input!

cues.zh: 现在对人们来说，买自己超大的太阳能阵列和电池、离网生活，已经是划算的了
cues.en: It’s cost-effective at this point for people to buy their own oversized solar arrays and batteries and live off-grid

cues.zh: 所以你到底为什么让人说服你，可再生能源难如登天、贵得离谱？
cues.en: so why the hell are you letting people convince you that renewable energy is impossibly difficult and expensive?

cues.zh: 抱歉，有点跑题了。
cues.en: Sorry, got a little off track there.

cues.zh: 呃，不过你应该了解一下我们国家种的玉米到底都用来干什么了。
cues.en: Uh, but you should look into what we actually do with all the corn we grow in this country.

cues.zh: 40% 不是给你吃的食物，甚至不是喂牲畜的——
cues.en: 40% of it isn’t food feeding you or even livestock-

cues.zh: 是用来喂汽车的！
cues.en: it’s for feeding cars!

cues.zh: 我们干得真棒！
cues.en: We’re doing real great!

cues.zh: 总之，厨房电器能带来的能效提升不多，
cues.en: Anyway, there aren’t many efficiency gains to be had from appliances in the kitchen,

cues.zh: 但你家里耗能大户，主要是暖通空调系统和水 heater，才是需要重点关注的地方。
cues.en: but the big energy draws of your home, mainly your HVAC system and your water heater, are important areas of focus.

cues.zh: 说到热泵，这是我最喜欢的东西，
cues.en: With heat pumps, my very favorite things,

cues.zh: 我们可以把热能从一个地方转移到另一个地方，而且用热泵能转移的热量比运行热泵所需的能量还多！
cues.en: we can move heat energy from one place to another and it turns out we can move more heat with a heat pump than it takes to run the heat pump!

cues.zh: 真正高效的热泵能把一瓦输入功率变成四五瓦的热量，具体取决于条件，
cues.en: Really efficient heat pumps can turn one watt of input power into 4 or 5 watts of heat depending on conditions,

cues.zh: 这可不是矩阵出了故障。
cues.en: and that’s no glitch in the matrix.

cues.zh: 这就是转移热能而非创造热能的力量！
cues.en: It’s the power of moving heat energy rather than creating it!

cues.zh: 这可不是矩阵出了故障。
cues.en: And that’s no glitch in the matrix.

cues.zh: 我可以整天聊热泵，但我就说一句我的标志性说法，给可能还不知道的人：
cues.en: Now I could talk about heat pumps all day but I will just say my trademark phrase for those who may not be aware of it:

cues.zh: 空调就是热泵！
cues.en: air conditioners are heat pumps!

cues.zh: 这意味着如果你有空调，恭喜你！
cues.en: This means if you have an air conditioner, congratulations!

cues.zh: 你就有了一台热泵！
cues.en: You've got a heat pump!

cues.zh: 它的工作原理就是从你家里收集热能，然后泵到室外。
cues.en: And that thing works by collecting heat energy from inside your home and pumping it outside.

cues.zh: 把空调变成“热泵”的唯一部件，就是一个叫换向阀的组件，它能让空调反向运行，
cues.en: The only thing that turns an air conditioner into a "heat pump" is a component called the reversing valve which allows that air conditioner to run in reverse,

cues.zh: 从室外收集热量并搬到室内。
cues.en: collecting heat from outside and moving it inside.

cues.zh: 这意味着同一台机器既能供暖又能制冷！
cues.en: And that means the same machine can provide heating and cooling!

cues.zh: 我这么说带着点无奈，因为热泵被吹捧成新技术，可实际上它是非常老的技术，
cues.en: I say this with frustration because heat pumps are touted as new technology when in fact it’s very old technology,

cues.zh: 唯一的新进展是，它们已经好到能在像我这样的寒冷气候里高效工作了。
cues.en: and the only new development is that they’ve become good enough to work effectively in cold climates like mine.

cues.zh: 然而许多暖通空调专业人士却拒绝接受这个事实。
cues.en: Yet many HVAC professionals refuse to read the memo.

cues.zh: 当然还有热泵热水器和热泵干衣机，它们的热效率也极高，
cues.en: Then of course there’s heat pump water heaters and heat pump clothes dryers which are also extremely thermally moving

cues.zh: 不过我要转到一个小东西，我们称之为“吸血鬼耗电”。
cues.en: but I’ll move on to a little thing we call vampire drain.

cues.zh: 许多电子设备从未真正关机，而是以极低的待机功耗运行。
cues.en: Many electronic devices are never truly off and instead operate at very low standby power levels.

cues.zh: 不过说实话，我们最近在这方面已经取得了很大进展，所以如今不太值得过多纠结了——
cues.en: Honestly, though, we’ve made great strides in this area lately so it’s not worth too much consideration these days -

cues.zh: 但另一方面，我们也有个习惯，就是会在家里到处摆放智能音箱、摄像头之类的小设备，它们耗电不算大，但积少成多。
cues.en: but on the other hand we also have a habit of sticking gadgets like smart speakers and cameras around the house which aren’t huge power draws but they add up.

cues.zh: 不过这些我先不管，我想聊点算起账来很有意思的事。
cues.en: I’ll ignore those, though, instead I want to talk about something which is very funny when you do the math.

cues.zh: 我的微波炉和很多微波炉一样，带一个时钟。
cues.en: My microwave, as do many, has a clock.

cues.zh: 为了显示时间，它要消耗0.7瓦。
cues.en: And to show the time it uses 0.7 watts.

cues.zh: 这意味着它光是当个时钟，每天就要消耗16.8瓦时。
cues.en: That means it consumes 16.8 watt-hours per day just being a clock.

cues.zh: 它加热食物时功率是1650瓦，但微波炉出名的地方就是加热特别快。
cues.en: Now it uses 1,650 watts when it’s heating stuff but microwaves are famously quite fast at that.

cues.zh: 这意味着，取决于我怎么用微波炉，它的时钟实际上可能比加热食物还费电。
cues.en: And that means depending on how I use my microwave, its clock can actually use more energy than microwaving things.

cues.zh: 我每天得用微波炉至少36.6秒来加热食物，才能和它时钟的耗电打平。
cues.en: I need to use the microwave at least 36.6 seconds every day to heat food just to break even with its clock.

cues.zh: 而且我并不是每天都用微波炉。
cues.en: And I don’t use my microwave every day.

cues.zh: 当然，我基本确定总体上时钟的耗电没那么重要，因为我用微波炉时通常会用好几分钟，
cues.en: Now, I’m pretty sure on net the clock is less significant since when I do use the microwave I’m often using it for several minutes,

cues.zh: 但确实有些日子我只用它化个黄油，这就意味着时钟耗的电更多。
cues.en: but there have absolutely been days when all I did was melt some butter meaning the clock used more energy.

cues.zh: 这不仅有趣，还应该让你意识到，微波炉加热食物是一种极其节能的方式。
cues.en: This is not only funny, but should also make you realize microwave ovens are an extremely energy-efficient way to heat food.

cues.zh: 你每次只用它几分钟，因为它实际上是在用辐射轰击食物，直接加热食物。
cues.en: You only use them for a few minutes at a time because they’re literally bombarding food with radiation and directly heating it.

cues.zh: 这简直是打了鸡血的感应加热！
cues.en: It’s induction cooking on steroids!

cues.zh: 但人们似乎常常不好意思用微波炉。
cues.en: Yet, people often seem ashamed of using microwave ovens.

cues.zh: 我觉得它们其实挺酷的。
cues.en: I think they’re pretty freakin’ neat.

cues.zh: 总之，该收尾了。
cues.en: But anywho, it’s time to wrap up.

cues.zh: 能源不一定非得是个神秘的东西。
cues.en: Energy doesn’t have to be a mysterious thing.

cues.zh: 没错，如今我们获取能源的方式确实非常复杂，
cues.en: Yes there’s a lot of complexity to how we obtain energy sources these days,

cues.zh: 我真心希望人们能走出熟悉的圈子，拥抱那些用一次也不会消失的能源的可能性。
cues.en: and I really hope people will step outside the familiar and embrace the possibilities of energy resources which don’t just disappear after you use them once.

cues.zh: 而不是像罐子里的丙烷那样用完就没了。
cues.en: Like all the propane in the bottle will.

cues.zh: 或者你加进汽车油箱里的所有汽油。
cues.en: Or all the gasoline you've ever put in a car's gas tank.

cues.zh: 抱歉，
cues.en: Sorry,

cues.zh: 呃，但你看，这正是我希望我们能多想想能源这件事的原因。
cues.en: Uh, but see, that’s really the whole reason I’d like us to be thinking about energy a little more.

cues.zh: 当我们能获得实际上近乎无限的能源，比如电网送来的电力时，
cues.en: When we have access to functionally limitless amounts of energy like electricity coming from a power grid,

cues.zh: 我们用了多少，真的很容易被忽视。
cues.en: how much we use is really easy to ignore.

cues.zh: 它不会像这个瓶子里的丙烷那样用完，我们只需担心账单上的数字。
cues.en: It’s not gonna run out like the propane in this bottle will, all we have to worry about is the number on a bill.

cues.zh: 但这不代表我们不该明智地使用它。
cues.en: But that doesn’t mean we shouldn't be wise about it.

cues.zh: 希望我已经帮你们认识到，直观理解功率和能量真的很有用。
cues.en: As I hope to have helped you see, an intuitive grasp of power and energy is really helpful.

cues.zh: 它能让你穿透所有的噪音。
cues.en: It allows you to cut through all the noise out there.

cues.zh: 比如，当有人说用电暖器能帮你省下取暖费。
cues.en: Like, for instance, when someone says using an electric space heater can save you money on your heating bills.

cues.zh: 当然，也许能，但大多数时候你听到的只是推销话术。
cues.en: Sure, it might, but most of the time you hear that it’s just a sales pitch.

cues.zh: 你得把家里其他地方的温度调低很多，才能抵消使用电暖器增加的成本。
cues.en: You need to turn the temperature way down in the rest of your home in order to offset the added cost of using a space heater.

cues.zh: 每次你遇到某种神奇的节能小玩意儿，那都是骗局。
cues.en: And every single time you run across some miracle energy-saving doodad, it’s a scam.

cues.zh: 降低电费没有什么奇招——能量就是能量。
cues.en: There isn’t one weird trick to lowering your energy bills - energy is energy.

cues.zh: 你的账单取决于你的用电行为，所以想降低账单，就得做出不同的选择。
cues.en: Your bills are based on what you do, so if you want to lower them you have to make different choices.

cues.zh: 当你了解功率与能量的关系时，你就有了做出这些选择所需的知识，
cues.en: And when you know how power relates to energy, you have the knowledge you need to make those choices,

cues.zh: 知道哪些选择真正重要、为什么重要，
cues.en: to know what choices actually matter and why,

cues.en: Well, you need to know how much power it can actually put out to determine what devices it can possibly run.

cues.en: And assuming it meets that need, then you need to know how much energy its battery pack can store to get a sense of what all it can do for you on one charge.

cues.zh: 最后，如果你知道自己冰箱一天到底用多少电，就能算出那组电池能让它撑多久。
cues.en: And finally, if you know how much energy, say, your refrigerator actually uses in a day, you’ll know how long that battery bank can keep it going.

cues.zh: 我想可以说，随着时间推移，这种理解会越来越必要——至少也是越来越有用。
cues.en: I think it’s fair to say that that sort of understanding is going to be increasingly necessary as time goes on - or at the very least, increasingly useful.
